traps.why: You handed over the magnesium alkoxide. Add H₃O⁺ to protonate it to the alcohol.
Acid before the carbonyl partner just protonates the Grignard: you get the alkane and no new C–C bond. Partner first, then H₃O⁺.
Formaldehyde adds only one carbon. Ethylene oxide adds two (the Grignard opens the ring).
That is only the product after step 1; it still needs 1. ethylene oxide; 2. H₃O⁺.

explanation: The Grignard opens ethylene oxide by SN2; H₃O⁺ protonates the alkoxide. Two extra carbons, 1° alcohol.

flaws.why: You handed over the magnesium alkoxide. Add H₃O⁺ to protonate it to the alcohol.
Step 1 (ethylene oxide) does nothing here: Make the Grignard first (Mg, dry ether), then add the carbonyl / epoxide partner.

distractors.name: cyclohexene
distractors.why: With 1. Mg, ether; 2. ethylene oxide; 3. H₃O⁺, cyclohexene gives a different product (shown).
